verdicts.reading: By end of 2022 the industrial-era corporation and its management model will have been replaced as the dominant form of economic organisation by digitally connected marketplaces (state of affairs, D30).
verdicts.mainstream_test: D30 state of affairs: by 2022 the largest economic actors are predominantly platform/marketplace organisations rather than traditional industrial-era corporations.
verdicts.reason: The text says 'will be replaced' (strong, dominant reading). In 2022 the largest firms by revenue were still mostly traditional industrial-era corporations (Walmart, State Grid, CNPC, Sinopec, Saudi Aramco, Volkswagen, CSCEC, CVS); only Amazon is a digital marketplace in the top 10. Digital platforms grew but did not displace the corporate form or its purpose. No reading of comparable faithfulness supports a hit; a weak 'partly displaced' reading would at most give partial, but it is not the text's wording.

evidence.title: Fortune Global 500 (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: 2022 top 10 by revenue: Walmart, Amazon, State Grid, CNPC, Sinopec, Saudi Aramco, Apple, Volkswagen, China State Construction, CVS Health; 9 of 10 are not marketplace platforms.

verdicts.reading: By end of 2022 at least one multinational will have deployed employee-facing software that detects a worker's frustration and automatically changes the tone/style of the feedback or guidance it gives that worker (event, D30, 'by Y').
verdicts.mainstream_test: D30 event: a documented deployment by a multinational of employee-facing tech that detects the worker's own frustration and adapts feedback tone, by 2022.
verdicts.reason: Emotion-AI coaching for employees was deployed at multinationals by 2018-2019 (Cogito at MetLife, Warwick RI call center): it reads voice signals in real time and nudges agents (e.g. coffee-cup cue for the agent's low energy). But the documented systems mainly read the customer's emotion and the agent's energy, and give fixed cues; I found no documented multinational deployment that detects the worker's frustration and automatically alters the tone/style of the guidance itself. Part of the stated event happened within the window.

evidence.title: Feeling emotional? The machines know (Boston Globe)
evidence.shows: MetLife began using Cogito in its Warwick, RI call center in 2018; it reads vocal tension, pitch and pace and gives agents visual cues (coffee cup for low energy, heart for caller's emotional state); supervisors see tallies.

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence at MetLife - Three Use Cases (Emerj)
evidence.shows: Cogito analyzes emotions in calls and suggests agents alter their tone toward the customer; framed as customer-emotion analysis, not adaptation of feedback to the worker's frustration.

evidence.title: Emotion Detection with AI (search result, where looked)
evidence.shows: Generic vendor claims that emotion AI detects overwhelmed agents and recommends breaks; no named multinational deployment adapting feedback tone to worker frustration found.

verdicts.reading: By end of 2020 there will exist whole business ecosystems in which participation requires using smart contracts (event/state of affairs, D30, 'by Y').
verdicts.mainstream_test: D30 state of affairs: at least one ecosystem (multi-party platform) live by 2020 whose participants must transact through smart contracts.
verdicts.reason: Both enterprise and public-chain readings are met. we.trade (12 European banks incl. HSBC, Deutsche Bank, Santander, UniCredit; IBM, Hyperledger Fabric) went live in 2018 as a trade finance platform whose trades execute via smart contracts. Ethereum DeFi, where all transactions are mediated by smart contracts, reached about $9B collateral by September 2020.

evidence.title: CaixaBank implements we.trade blockchain platform (Finextra)
evidence.shows: we.trade bank consortium platform in production, built on Hyperledger Fabric with smart contracts linking buyer, seller, their banks and transporter, auto-payment when conditions are met.

evidence.title: Helping companies trade seamlessly (IBM case study, we.trade)
evidence.shows: we.trade launched 2018 by a consortium of 12 banks; trade process executed on the platform's smart contracts.

evidence.title: Decentralized finance (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: DeFi transactions are mediated by smart contract programs; Bloomberg reported DeFi collateral of $9B in September 2020.
